sentences.text: + CRL.M.C. 3538/2023  SANDEEP GUPTA & ORS.

Through: Mr. Umesh Mish  Agarwal, Advs.
 petitioners in  versus  GOVT. OF NCT, DELHI & ANR. 
 Through: Ms. Richa Dhaw  with SI Vinod   Kailash- I.
 CORAM:
 HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE VIKAS MAHAJAN  ORDER  % 17.05.2023

1. The present petition has been file  quashing of the  498A/406/323/342/348/330/352/506/509/354(A)/34 IPC registered at Police Station Greater Kailash, on the ground that the parties have arrived at a settlement.
2. Issue notice.
The learned APP for the State accepts notice.

3. The learned APP for the State submits that since the settlement has taken place and the FIR is an outcome of a matrimonial dispute, the State has no objection, in case the FIR in question is quashed.
4. The petitioner no.1 (former husband) along with all other petitioners who are the family members of the petitioner no.1, as well as respondent no.2 are present in court.
The petitioners and the respondent no.2 have been identified by their respective counsels as well as by the Investigating Officer(I.O), SI Vinod Bhati, PS. Greater Kailash, New Delhi.
This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.
The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 24/09/2023 at 11:40:31 5.

The brief facts of the case are that the marriage between the parties was solemnised on 01.12.1989, as per Hindu Rites and Ceremonies, out of this wedlock, two sons namely Ishaan Gupta and Iraaj Gupta were born on 09.02.1991 and 08.09.1994, respectively.

1 6.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: On account of temperamental differences and indifferent attitudes, both the parties could not live together as husband and wife, as a result of which the respondent no.2 had been living separately since 07.09.2019.

Subsequently, with the intervention of family members, relatives and well- wishers, a settlement was arrived at between the petitioner no.1 and the respondent no.2, the terms whereof were reduced in writing in the form of settlement deed dated 20.03.2023.
In terms of the aforesaid settlement, the parties agreed to dissolve their marriage by decree of divorce by mutual consent.

7. The attention of the court is invited to Annexure P-3 to submit that the marriage between the parties has been dissolved by a decree of divorce by mutual consent with effect from 11.05.2023.
8.

It was further agreed by the parties that the petitioner shall pay an amount of Rs.30 lacs to the respondent no.2 towards all her claims relating to stree dhan, permanent maintenance and alimony whether past, present and future.
Out of the said amount, an amount of Rs.20 lacs has already been paid by the petitioner no.1 to the respondent no.2, the receipt of which respondent no.2 acknowleges.

The remaining amount of Rs.10 lacs has been paid by way of Demand Draft bearing no.031740 dated 15.05.2023 drawn in favour of respondent no. 2 drawn on Axis Bank, Greater Kailash II, Delhi (DL) which has been handed over by the petitioner no.1 to the respondent no.2 in the court today.
This is a digitally signed order.
The authenticity of the order can be re-verified from Delhi High Court Order Portal by scanning the QR code shown above.
The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 24/09/2023 at 11:40:31 9.
The respondent no.2, who is present in court today states that she has no objection, in case the FIR is quashed.

10. Having regard to the fact that the parties have already settled their disputes and have decided to move on in their life, no useful purpose will be served in continuing the criminal proceedings, rather the same would create further acrimony between them.
11. It is, thus, in the interest of justice that the present FIR and all the other proceedings emanating therefrom be quashed.
12. In view of the above, there is no legal impediment in quashing the present FIR in question.

A c c o r d i n g l y , F I R N o . 7 5 / 2 0 2 0 u n d e r S e c t i o n s 498A/406/323/342/348/330/352/506/509/354(A)/34 IPC registered at Police Station Greater Kailash is quashed along with all other consequential proceedings emanating therefrom.
13. The petition stands disposed off, in the above terms.
14. Order be uploaded on the website of this court.
